title: Kubernetes: security context, admission policies and limits

videos.script: Lesson nine hardened the way linkbox runs. But every one of those protections was a flag on a command somebody typed. {{flags}} A cluster can do better. It can refuse whatever leaves the flags out, for everybody, every time. {{refuse}} You will build one on your machine, with kind, and teach it to pull from your own registry. {{cluster}} Then the namespace gets the restricted profile. A pod that does not promise to behave is turned away. And a Deployment, you will see, can be let in while its pods are not. {{psa}} linkbox's manifest sets each field, one by one, and the pod runs with nothing it does not need. {{manifest}} Two rules of your own come next, checked by the API server itself. Images only from your registry. A memory limit on every container. {{rules}} And last, the budget. What one container may ask for, and what the whole namespace may use. {{budget}}
